# hosttracker_status_page (Resource)

A public status page: the components you publish, the incidents you declare against them, and the appearance the page renders in.

The component set is written as a WHOLE. Terraform sends the list in `components` in full on every change, and a component the list omits is removed from the page - so either let Terraform own the set, or leave the attribute out entirely and manage components in the web app.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hosttracker_monitor" "marketing" {
  type = "http"
  url  = "https://example.com/"
  name = "Marketing site"

  locations = {
    pools = ["allworld"]
  }
}

resource "hosttracker_monitor" "api" {
  type = "http"
  url  = "https://api.example.com/health"
  name = "API"

  locations = {
    pools = ["allworld"]
  }
}

# A public status page. The component list is a snapshot: every save
# replaces the whole set, in the order written here, and a component the
# list omits is removed from the page.
resource "hosttracker_status_page" "acme" {
  slug  = "acme-status"
  title = "Acme status"

  settings = {
    homepage_url = "https://example.com"
    theme        = "light"
    theme_color  = "#2f6feb"
    density      = "wide"
    show_groups  = true
    robots_index = true
    language     = "en"
    sla_target   = 99.9

    # The WHOLE feature set: a feature not listed here is off.
    features = ["barCharts", "uptimePercent", "outageDetails", "subscribe"]

    # Leave this off while Terraform owns the components: a monitor the
    # API adds by itself is a component the next plan proposes to remove.
    auto_add_monitors = false
  }

  components = [
    {
      monitor_id = hosttracker_monitor.marketing.id
      group      = "Public"
    },
    {
      monitor_id = hosttracker_monitor.api.id
      name       = "Public API"
      group      = "Public"
    },
    # A dependency this account does not monitor. Its state is pinned by
    # hand, so changing it is an apply.
    {
      third_party  = true
      name         = "Payments provider"
      group        = "Dependencies"
      manual_state = "operational"
    },
  ]
}

output "acme_status_page" {
  value = hosttracker_status_page.acme.public_url
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `slug` (String) The page's permanent public address: lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, 3 to 64 characters, unique across the product. It cannot be changed, so editing it replaces the page - which frees the old slug and takes the page's incidents and subscribers with it.
- `title` (String) The heading the public page carries, at most 200 characters.

### Optional

- `components` (Attributes List) The components the page publishes, in display order. Leave the attribute out to let the web app own the set; write it, and every save replaces the whole set.

A component is either MONITORED - it names a `monitor_id` and takes its state from that monitor's checks - or THIRD-PARTY: `third_party = true`, its own `name`, and a `manual_state` you pin by hand. The provider matches each entry against the page's existing rows (by monitor for a monitored one, by name for a third-party one) so that per-component subscriptions survive a save. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--components))
- `settings` (Attributes) How the public page looks and behaves. Every member is optional and also computed: a member the configuration leaves out keeps the value it has, because the API reads an absent member as "leave this alone". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings))

### Read-Only

- `component_count` (Number) How many components the page publishes.
- `created` (Number) When the page was created, in Unix seconds.
- `custom_domain` (String) The custom domain as configured, when there is one. Activation is dashboard bookkeeping and is not managed here.
- `has_password` (Boolean) Whether the page is behind a password. The password itself is set in the web app, not here.
- `id` (String) The page's id.
- `public_url` (String) Where the page is served from: `https://status.host-tracker.com/<slug>`, or the custom domain when one is configured. The provider composes it; the API does not publish it.
- `unresolved_incidents` (Number) How many of the page's declared incidents are still open.

<a id="nestedatt--components"></a>
### Nested Schema for `components`

Optional:

- `group` (String) The heading this component is listed under, at most 100 characters. Components with no group are listed first.
- `manual_state` (String) The state pinned on a THIRD-PARTY component: `operational`, `degraded` or `down`. A monitored component's state comes from its checks, and the API refuses this there.
- `monitor_id` (String) The monitor whose state this component shows. Required unless `third_party`.
- `name` (String) The label shown on the page, at most 200 characters. Required on a third-party component; a monitored one inherits its monitor's name when this is left out.
- `third_party` (Boolean) True for a component this account does not monitor - a dependency you report on by hand.


<a id="nestedatt--settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `settings`

Optional:

- `announcement` (String) A banner shown above the components, at most 500 characters. Write `""` to remove it.
- `auto_add_monitors` (Boolean) Add newly created monitors to this page automatically. Leave it off when Terraform owns `components`: a monitor the API adds by itself is a component the next plan proposes to remove.
- `dark_logo_url` (String) The logo used when the page renders dark.
- `density` (String) How tightly the component rows are packed: `wide` or `compact`.
- `favicon_url` (String) The icon browsers show for the page.
- `features` (Set of String) The page's WHOLE feature set - writing it replaces what is there, and a feature not listed is off. One of `barCharts`, `uptimePercent`, `outageDetails`, `detailsPages`, `floatingBar`, `monitorUrls`, `hidePaused`, `overallUptime`, `downtimeFeed`, `subscribe`.
- `google_analytics_id` (String) A Google Analytics measurement id (`G-XXXXXXXX`).
- `header_bg_color` (String) The header's background colour, spelled `#rrggbb`.
- `header_text_color` (String) The header's text colour, spelled `#rrggbb`.
- `hide_branding` (Boolean) Hide the HostTracker attribution, where the plan allows it.
- `homepage_url` (String) Where the page's logo and title link to.
- `language` (String) The language the public page is rendered in: `en`, `cs`, `de`, `es`, `fr`, `it`, `ja`, `nl`, `pl`, `pt`, `ru`, `tr`, `ua`, `zh`.
- `logo_alignment` (String) Where the logo sits in the header: `left` or `center`.
- `logo_url` (String) The logo shown at the top of the page.
- `robots_index` (Boolean) Allow search engines to index the public page.
- `show_groups` (Boolean) Render components under their group headings.
- `sla_target` (Number) The uptime percentage the page measures its components against, between 0 and 100. Leave it out for each monitor's own target.
- `theme` (String) Which palette the page renders in: `light` or `dark`.
- `theme_color` (String) The page's accent colour, spelled `#rrggbb`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A status page is imported by its id, which the `hosttracker_status_page`
# data source resolves from the slug:
#
#   data "hosttracker_status_page" "acme" { slug = "acme-status" }
#
terraform import hosttracker_status_page.acme 6b1f2a70-3c8e-4d51-9f2a-7c4e5d6b8a90

# The component set comes with it, in display order. Write the components
# out in the configuration to match, or leave the attribute off and manage
# them in the web app.
```
